note: Who names a split browser file in code and needs more than a tag in a page or the reader of the tests to keep working, and how each does. Read by tools/restructure/browser-consumers.mjs: a file that is named somewhere not listed here cannot be split. `keeps` lists declarations that stay in the file because the consumer reads them there.

tools/site-shots/scenes.mjs.how: Reads DASHBOARD_LAYOUT_VERSION out of the file as text, so that declaration stays in it.

server/test/settings-load-order.test.mjs.how: Reads the split through the reader, and one of its checks says defaultNewsFeedsClient sits below the line that loads the settings, so that function stays in the file.

server/js/settings.js.server/test/restructure-engine-test-read: Names the file only inside sample test text it hands to the tool that re-points tests; it never opens it.

server/test/classic-script-globals.test..how: Reads every script of a page as its own file, never through the reader, and names this file as one of the two that may both declare cssId, so cssId stays in it.

server/test/pages-logic.test.mjs.how: Loads the file as a Node module for the functions it exports, which use nothing else of the file, so they stay in it.

server/test/tabgroups-logic.test.mjs.how: Loads the file as a Node module for the functions it exports, which use only each other and three small helpers, so all of them stay in it.

server/js/dashboard-tabgroups.js.server/test/tile-tab-colors.test.mjs: Loads the file as a Node module for tabColorVars, which stays in it (see tabgroups-logic.test.mjs).
server/js/dashboard-tabgroups.js.server/test/grid-logic.test.mjs: Loads the file as a Node module for functions that stay in it (see tabgroups-logic.test.mjs).
